keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 600-999: infobox 'c. 600-c. 1000'; the page gives the core as 'the southern Lake Titicaca Basin', the Moquegua Valley (about 150 km from the lake, 'flourished 400-1100') and colonies up to about 300 km away, without dates or a total area. A 100 km disc round the site stands for the core and a 30 km disc for Moquegua (my reading). Recent research 'questions whether it was either' a state or an empire.

ledger.note: c. 600: Tiwanaku rises as the regional power of the southern Titicaca basin. Infobox 'c. 600-c. 1000'; 'large parts of the city were rebuilt around 600' and the population grew rapidly from about 600 to 800; other settlements had been abandoned between 450 and 550. The Tiwanaku page: site 'founded around AD 110'.

ledger.note: c. 1000: Tiwanaku collapses. 'Appeared to have collapsed around AD 1000' (Tiwanaku page); ceramic production stopped about 1000 and the Moquegua colony and the urban core were abandoned within a few decades; a severe drought is the proposed cause, which later chronologies dispute. The Lupaca page: the Lupaca and other Aymara peoples 'formed powerful kingdoms after the collapse of the Tiwanaku Empire in the 11th century'.

notes: The page questions that Tiwanaku was a state or empire at all; typed 'state' because the article is titled Tiwanaku Empire. Cliopatria has no Tiwanaku row. No area is given on either page (city 4 km2). Colonies up to about 300 km away (coastal Peru, northern Chile cemeteries, the Azapa Valley, the Yungas, northern Argentina) are named without dates and are not drawn; San Pedro de Atacama and Cochabamba do not appear on the pages. Moquegua overlaps the Wari disc (the page: 'coexisted at Moquegua without conflict'). The Moquegua colony 'flourished 400-1100' against a state starting 600: kept in from the start. Pariti Island ceramics 900-1050. A conjectured southward migration after the collapse is undated. The List of wars involving the Inca Empire page dates Aymara invasions of Tiwanaku and a Tiwanaku civil war to the 12th century, after the collapse about 1000 on the two Tiwanaku pages; the pages' 1000 is kept.
